target: मैंने आज पाँच पत्र लिखे हैं।
english: I have written five letters today.
tip: With ने (ne), the past verb matches the thing acted on: लिखे (likhe) is plural to agree with पाँच पत्र (paanch patra = five letters), not with 'I'.

target: अभी सुबह के नौ बजे हैं।
english: It is nine o'clock in the morning now.
tip: O'clock is plural: नौ बजे हैं (nau baje hain = nine have struck), with हैं not है. Only one o'clock is singular – एक बजा है (ek baja hai).

target: बारह बजकर चालीस मिनट पर बस आएगी।
english: The bus will come at 12:40.
tip: Minutes past the hour use बजकर (bajkar = having struck): बारह बजकर चालीस मिनट (baarah bajkar chaalees minute) = 12:40.

target: मैं आठ बजे तक घर पहुँच जाऊँगा।
english: I'll be home by eight.
tip: तक (tak) covers both 'by' and 'until': आठ बजे तक (aath baje tak) = by eight here. With deadlines it's 'by'; with ongoing actions it's 'until'.

target: मेरे दो बेटे और एक बेटी है।
english: I have two sons and one daughter.
tip: Hindi has no verb 'have'. Family is stated as simply yours: मेरे दो बेटे और एक बेटी है (mere do bete aur ek beti hai = my two sons and one daughter are).

target: मैंने पिछले साल दो लाख रुपये बचाए।
english: I saved two lakh rupees last year.
tip: Hindi counts big money in लाख (laakh = 100,000): दो लाख रुपये (do laakh rupaye) = 200,000 rupees. After thousand, the everyday unit is lakh, not 'hundred thousand'.

target: मुझे दो टिकटों की ज़रूरत है।
english: I need two tickets.
tip: Plural noun before a position word takes oblique -ों: दो टिकटों की (do tikaton ki = of two tickets).

target: यह ट्रेन बारह डिब्बों वाली एक्सप्रेस है।
english: This is an express train with twelve coaches.
tip: वाली (vali) turns a noun into 'the one with': बारह डिब्बों वाली (baarah dibbon vali) = the twelve-coach one. Hindi builds adjectives from nouns this way.

target: पौने दो बजे मैं दफ़्तर पहुँच जाता हूँ।
english: I reach the office at one forty-five.
tip: पौने (paune) subtracts a quarter from the hour named: पौने दो बजे (paune do baje) = 1:45, not 2:45. Hindi points at the hour that's coming.

target: मेरे पास सिर्फ़ पचास रुपये हैं।
english: I only have fifty rupees.
tip: Owned things take पास: मेरे पास सिर्फ़ पचास रुपये हैं (mere paas sirf pachaas rupaye hain = by me are only fifty rupees). Family skips पास – bare मेरे (mere) for relatives.

target: मैंने यह फ़ोन बारह हज़ार रुपये में ख़रीदा।
english: I bought this phone for twelve thousand rupees.
tip: Prices take में (mein = in): बारह हज़ार रुपये में ख़रीदा (baarah hazaar rupaye mein khareeda = bought in 12,000 rupees). Hindi says 'in' where English says 'for'.

target: यह दवा दिन में तीन बार लेनी है।
english: This medicine has to be taken three times a day.
tip: 'Three times a day' is said with में (mein = in): दिन में तीन बार (din mein teen baar). बार (baar) is the word for 'times'.

target: हमारे गाँव में एक सौ से अधिक घर हैं।
english: There are more than one hundred houses in our village.
tip: से (se) means 'from' but also handles 'than': सौ से अधिक (sau se adhik = more than a hundred) is literally 'from a hundred, more'.

target: दो सौ ग्राम चीनी और आधा किलो आटा दो।
english: Give two hundred grams sugar and half kilo flour.
tip: Measures attach directly, no 'of': दो सौ ग्राम चीनी (do sau gram cheeni = two hundred grams sugar). Nothing sits between the amount and the noun.

target: आज सुबह पाँच बजे से ही मेरी नींद खुल गई।
english: I woke up as early as five this morning.
tip: The tiny word ही (hi) means 'as early as / right from': पाँच बजे से ही (paanch baje se hi = from five itself). Without ही it's just neutral 'from five'.

target: एक साल में तीन सौ पैंसठ दिन होते हैं।
english: There are three hundred sixty-five days in a year.
tip: दिन (din = day) looks the same in singular and plural: तीन सौ पैंसठ दिन (teen sau painsath din = 365 days). Masculine nouns ending in a consonant do not change in the direct plural.

target: ट्रैफ़िक जाम की वजह से हमें एक घंटा लग गया।
english: It took us one hour because of the traffic jam.
tip: Time acts on you: हमें एक घंटा लग गया (hamein ek ghanta lag gaya = to us one hour attached). The hour is the subject; you are the target of the delay.

target: इस स्कूल को १९५० में खोला गया था।
english: This school was opened in 1950.
tip: Devanagari has its own digits: १९५० (1950). Indian signs, dates and prices switch between १२३ and 123 freely, so both sets are worth knowing.

target: आज पच्चीसवीं तारीख़ है और महीने के पाँच दिन बचे हैं।
english: Today is the twenty-fifth and five days of the month are left.
tip: Ordinals agree in gender: तारीख़ (taareekh = date) is feminine, so 'twenty-fifth' is पच्चीसवीं (pachchisvin) with -वीं, not पच्चीसवाँ.

target: उन्नीस सौ सैंतालीस में भारत आज़ाद हुआ।
english: India became independent in 1947.
tip: Hindi keeps 'hundred' audible in years: उन्नीस सौ सैंतालीस (unnees sau saintalees = nineteen hundred forty-seven). English drops it – 'nineteen forty-seven'.

target: इस तालाब की गहराई कम से कम बीस फ़ीट है।
english: The depth of this pond is at least twenty feet.
tip: कम से कम (kam se kam = less than less) means 'at least': कम से कम बीस फ़ीट (kam se kam bees feet) = at least twenty feet. The doubling sets a floor.

target: मीठे फल बच्चों को बहुत पसंद आते हैं।
english: Children like sweet fruits very much.
tip: Liking flips in Hindi: fruits come pleasing TO the kids – बच्चों को (bachchon ko) पसंद आते हैं (pasand aate hain). The verb agrees with the fruits, not the likers.

target: इस मंदिर को बनने में पाँच साल लगे।
english: It took five years to build this temple.
tip: 'It took five years' has no 'took': बनने में पाँच साल लगे (banne mein paanch saal lage) = 'in being built, five years attached'. Time spent uses लगना (lagna = attach).

target: शनिवार को हमारी छुट्टी होती है।
english: We have a holiday on Saturdays.
tip: Days take को (ko) where English says 'on': शनिवार को (shanivaar ko) = on Saturday. Hindi has no separate word for 'on' with days – को does that job.

target: शिक्षिका ने बच्चों को कविता सुनाई।
english: The teacher recited a poem to the children.
tip: When the receiver has को (ko), the verb tracks the thing given: सुनाई (sunaai) is feminine to match कविता (kavita = poem) – not the teacher, not the children.

target: घर पहुँचते ही मुझे फ़ोन करना।
english: Call me as soon as you reach home.
tip: -ते ही (te hi) = the instant it happens: पहुँचते ही (pahunchte hi) = the moment you arrive. English needs 'as soon as'; Hindi bolts ही onto the verb.

target: बड़े भैया कैसे हैं? उनको मेरा प्रणाम।
english: How is elder brother? My regards to him.
tip: One respected elder, plural pronoun: उनको (unko = to them) for बड़े भैया (bade bhaiya = elder brother). Singular उसको (usko) here would sound disrespectful.

target: किताब छपेगी तो लेखक को रॉयल्टी मिलेगी।
english: The author will get royalty when the book is printed.
tip: 'Will get' flips: the royalty is the subject – रॉयल्टी मिलेगी (royalty milegi = will be received) – and the receiver takes को: लेखक को (lekhak ko = to the author).

target: मेरा पालतू कुत्ता अजनबियों को देखकर भौंकता है।
english: My pet dog barks when he sees strangers.
tip: -कर (kar) chains actions into one word: अजनबियों को देखकर (ajnabiyon ko dekhkar) = 'having seen strangers' – where English needs a whole 'when he sees' clause.

target: मुझे कल छुट्टी लेनी है।
english: I need to take tomorrow off.
tip: 'I need to' is 'to me': मुझे कल छुट्टी लेनी है (mujhe kal chhutti leni hai) = to-me tomorrow leave to-take is. Needs land on you via मुझे (mujhe), not a verb like 'must'.
